headline: Google DeepMind reports a human-steered Antigravity workflow for antimicrobial-peptide candidate search
summary: Google DeepMind’s 15 October walkthrough describes a researcher-steered Antigravity/Gemini 3.8 Flash workflow that searches UniProt candidates, cross-checks sequence similarity, compares predicted structures and genomic context, and prepares a wet-lab protocol. The example names UniProt A0A0U0D591, a 97-amino-acid protein assigned to the Lactococcin 972 family; the company says the candidate and others are undergoing wet-lab validation. This is a first-party account of a computational candidate-selection workflow, not evidence of antibacterial efficacy or independent discovery performance.
